author: reek
body: A real triangle mesh, ray-traced from Codex [Device] AST. The host uploads an icosahedron (20 triangles, 9 fixed-point coordinates each) into a storage buffer; one GPU thread per pixel inverse-rotates its ray into the mesh frame, then folds over the triangles reading each one's vertices from the buffer and running a Moller-Trumbore ray-triangle test, keeping the nearest hit. The winner is re-read to build its face normal, and the facet is flat-shaded two-sided with a per-face colour. This is the reference site's "glTF" technique -- arbitrary mesh geometry from a buffer, reached through the storage-pointer helper parameter feature (the force loop of the N-body demo, now over geometry).

author: reek
body: Fold over the mesh reading each triangle's nine coordinates from the buffer (storage pointer) and Moller-Trumbore testing it; returns the nearest tri id.

author: reek
body: Per pixel: build the ray, inverse-rotate into the mesh frame, find the nearest triangle, re-read its vertices for the flat face normal, and two-sided shade.
